summary: Gone: a 1934 CCC-built steel Aermotor tower and ground cabin on the Klamath reservation, used in emergencies into the 1960s; removal year unknown.

facts.status_note: Used for emergencies into the 1960s; the register, firelookout.com and the Klamath blog say it is gone. No source gives the year it came down.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Reported heights: 61 ft (firetower.org, firelookout.com), 60 ft (Klamath blog), 67 ft (Oregon Lookouts, 1934 and 1959 entries). The brief's 20.4 m equals 67 ft. No height_m is set because the sources disagree.
firetower.org says built in the 1930s; the Klamath blog and Oregon Lookouts give 1934. The story uses 1934.

firetower.org and firelookout.com place it in the Fremont National Forest, and the register's administration line reads U.S.Forest Service (the brief's value). The Klamath blog and Oregon Lookouts name the Klamath Indian Agency as a managing agency, with the Oregon Department of Forestry and the Fremont NF.

notes_for_editor: No source gives the year the tower came down, so no removed event is recorded. No source describes remains or public access today; access is not set. Coordinates: the firetower.org/FFLOS point (42.643110, -121.126060) matches the brief's FFLOS record; the brief's second point (west_us_lookouts) was not checked. The brief's height_m (20.4) is only one of three reported heights. The brief's agency line is incomplete: the blog and Oregon Lookouts name the Klamath Indian Agency as the first managing agency. Photos on firetower.org (credited to Ron Kemnow and Howard Verschoor) not recorded: no licence stated.
